question: Two resistances A and B of 10Ω and 20Ω are connected in series with a 6 V battery. If V₁ and V₂ are the potential drops across A and B respectively, and I₁ and I₂ are the currents flowing through them, then (V₁/V₂) and (I₁/I₂) are □( ) respectively.
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When resistances are connected in series, the same current flows through each resistor.
 
• The potential drop across a resistor in a series circuit is directly proportional to its resistance.
 
• The ratio of potential drops (V₁/V₂) across resistors A and B is equal to the ratio of their resistances (R₁/R₂).
 
• The ratio of currents (I₁/I₂) through resistors in series is always 1 because the current is the same through all series components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Series Circuit:**

 
 
• A series circuit is a type of electrical circuit in which there is only one path for the current to flow.
 
• All components are connected end-to-end, forming a single pathway for current flow.
 
• The current (I) is the same through each component in the circuit.
 
• The total resistance (R_total) of the circuit is the sum of the individual resistances: R_total = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rn.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• It is mathematically expressed as V = IR, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Potential Drop:**
 
 
• The potential drop (voltage drop) across a resistor in a circuit is the amount of voltage lost as the electric current flows through the resistor.
 
• In a series circuit, the potential drop across each resistor is different and depends on the resistance of each resistor.
 
 
 
• **Resistors in Series:**
 
 
• When resistors are connected in series, the same current flows through each resistor.
 
• The total voltage across the series combination is the sum of the voltages across each individual resistor: V_total = V₁ + V₂ + ... + Vn.
 
• The voltage drop across each resistor can be found using Ohm's Law: V = IR.
 
• The voltage drop ratio (V₁/V₂) is equal to the resistance ratio (R₁/R₂).
